$why: Every WORKLIST_* environment name this repository reads, in one place, so that a name nobody reads and a read nobody registered are both findings.

THE DEFECT: a typo'd name reads as UNSET. For a flag that defaults to `on` -- WORKLIST_FOCUS today, and until 2026-10-04 WORKLIST_AGENT_HINT, WORKLIST_AGENT_PUSHBACK and WORKLIST_CADENCE, which moved to agent/plans/QUEUE.md -- that is the FAIL-OPEN direction: the author believes they switched something off and it is still running. Nothing in the tree said so before 2026-09-09.

Measured 2026-09-09 against the bash corpus that has since been ported to pytest: 133 live names across 60 tracked files at 183 read sites. The plan box said 134, which is the GREP answer; one of those, WORKLIST_EMAIL, appeared only in a comment describing a name that no longer existed, which is why this scanner counts READS rather than greps.

Enforced by check:ci-worklist-env-registry, both directions. The name set and each name's default spellings are DERIVED from the code by the gate and pinned here, so this file cannot drift into being a description of what somebody once intended. `kind`, `class` and `why` are the authored fields, and the gate checks each against the derived shape or its allowed set.

`class` (harness or gate-seam) is the field `.ci/config/env-manifest.json` is rendered from: every WORKLIST_* member of its shard lists is generated from this file, which makes this file the one authored home of a WORKLIST_* name. `foreign_reads` holds the names read only where this scan cannot look (a TypeScript gate), each with its reader and a reason, and the gate proves the reader still names it. Register a name with `npm run env:register -- <module> <NAME> --class <c> --kind <k> --default <spelling>... [--why <w>]`, which writes this file, re-renders the manifest and runs the three registry gates.

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_roster.py.why: the parallel-writer roster's limits are the operator's (4 writers by default and a `writer_cap:` line in agent/plans/QUEUE.md, a 20-minute status ping, 2026-09-24, 'no escape hatches'), so no variable may retune them and a registered knob would be exactly the hatch that was ruled out

.claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/block_agent.why: the PreToolUse half of the same writer cap; it calls `wl_roster.writer_cap`, and an environment read here would let a spawn bypass the cap the Stop hook enforces

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_standdown.py.why: the stand-down keep-lists (the cap-saturated wait and focus mode) decide which checks still block while the session is told to wait; a variable that retuned a list or the focus batch and expiry limits would be exactly the escape hatch the roster rules out

.claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/block_focus.why: the PreToolUse half of focus mode: it refuses writer spawns while a PR wind-down is declared, and an environment read here would let a spawn bypass the focus the Stop hook enforces

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_planconc.py.why: plan priority order and the plan-concurrency rules (the mutex and the Owns overlap, operator 2026-09-25 section X); a variable that retuned what counts as an overlap, or which lease counts as live, would be an escape hatch around the pre-agent guard and the roster that read it

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_planorder.py.why: the one plan order and concurrency hold every next-item picker reads (queue-slot, the guide, the open list, the backlog nomination, the queue lease beside a free slot); a variable that decided which item is held or which plan ranks first would be an escape hatch around the pre-agent guard and the roster

.claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/block_plan_.why: the PreToolUse half of plan concurrency: it refuses a writer spawn that breaks a live exclusive plan or claims files a live plan owns, and an environment read here would let a spawn bypass it

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_gh.py.why: the Stop hook's one gh layer (agent/plans/PLAN-ci-consolidation.md Part C): the transient-retry bound of two attempts and one 2 s pause (PLAN-gh-retry G13) and the per-spawn timeout decide how much of every stop's budget a slow or failing GitHub may spend, so no variable may stretch them

exclusions.agent/: invariant 7: agent/ is live gated state (.claude/hooks/stop/wl_store.py:274), not source. It is full of plans and briefs that NAME these variables in prose, and admitting it would register every name any plan ever discussed. Declared here rather than hardcoded in the gate so the reason travels with the exclusion.
exclusions.docs/: prose about the program, not the program. Same argument as agent/: a documented name is not a read, and a gate that treats it as one can never report a name as dead.

kinds.flag: a toggle. A typo reads as the default, which for a flag defaulting to `on` is FAIL-OPEN. `why` is REQUIRED, and every default must be one of on, off, 1, 0 or empty.
kinds.tuning: a numeric threshold, limit, count or timeout. A typo yields the default, which is fail-safe, so no `why` is required. Every default must parse as a number.
kinds.path: a directory or file location. Named `*_DIR`/`*_ROOT`, or a default containing a path separator.
kinds.handle: an identity supplied by the harness or the environment: a session id, a pid, a branch, a ref. Unset is the normal state and means `work it out`, so a typo turns a capability off silently. `why` is REQUIRED.
kinds.corpus: a pattern, list or model id that selects WHAT the program looks at or uses. Narrowing one does not make a check stricter, it makes it see less, which is the vacuity direction. `why` is REQUIRED, and this kind is deliberately the residual so that the residual cannot become a dumping ground.

WORKLIST_AGENT_BRANCH.why: The branch the worklist attributes work to, overriding the `git symbolic-ref` read in wl_core.py:573. A handle rather than a flag: unset is the normal state and means `ask git`. It is also the most-assigned name in the test corpus, which is why a typo here surfaces as a test that quietly reads the real branch.

WORKLIST_CI_RETRY_PATTERNS.why: The comma-separated job-name patterns wl_ci.py:176 will auto-retry. A corpus, not a knob: adding a pattern widens what the hook is willing to re-run on the operator's behalf, so the value is a policy decision and the default is four named job families.

WORKLIST_FOCUS.why: FAIL-OPEN ON A TYPO: defaults to `on`, and the fail-open direction is OFF, not on. wl_checks.py:5484 checks it only on the path where every violation is about to be rendered (the fail-safe reggate emit); a misspelled name reads as unset, the default `on` applies, and the caller gets the full render it already asked for by default -- a typo here cannot silently suppress output, only fail to suppress it.

WORKLIST_HARNESS_PID.why: The harness pid, overriding the ancestor walk in wl_liveness.py:172, for tests and for setups where the walk cannot see the harness. Read with `.isdigit()`, so a typo and a non-numeric value are indistinguishable from unset and both fall back to the walk.

WORKLIST_JUDGE.why: test seam only: standing on/off is agent/plans/QUEUE.md `judge:`, and env `on` or `off` overrides it (wl_judge.disabled). Any other value is ignored, so a misspelled value falls back to QUEUE.md rather than disabling a paid call.

WORKLIST_JUDGE_MODEL.why: The model id for the judge call, wl_judge.py:24. Pinned to a dated haiku build rather than an alias, because cost and latency were measured against that build ($0.011-$0.026 warm) and an alias would silently move both.

WORKLIST_LKG_CHILD.why: The last-known-good recursion guard (wl_lkg.py, agent/plans/PLAN-stop-hook-continuity.md P2.5), set only by worklist.py on the snapshot child it spawns after a live-tree crash. Unset is the normal state. A misspelled read would read as unset inside the child, so a crashing snapshot would try to fall back again; the child's own crash then emits the ordinary crash block, which is the fail-closed direction.

WORKLIST_PROFILE.why: `off` disables the tier-0 resource profiler (wl_resprofile.py:197 and :369). Compared with `== "off"` in both places, so every other spelling leaves profiling on. Classed as a corpus rather than a flag because the bash side reads it with a different default spelling, which is itself worth seeing in this table.

WORKLIST_PROGRAM_SURFACE.why: The space-separated tree list wl_checks.py:70 treats as `the program`, split() into three roots. A corpus and not a path: it is one string holding several bare directory NAMES with no separator in any of them, and narrowing it does not make any check stricter, it makes the check see less of the program. The gate caught this entry classed as a path on its first run against the real tree, which is the shape rule doing its job.

WORKLIST_PUBLISH_REF.why: The ref a PR is published on, wl_ci.py:42 and :77. Empty means the session has not opted in and pays nothing; when it IS set and the lookup fails, that is reported as a hook-side inability rather than passing quietly. A typo therefore silently opts the session out.

WORKLIST_REGISTRY_OVERRIDE_FILE.why: GATE-SEAM, test-only: an absolute path, read by check:ci-worklist-env-registry's own run() in place of the real .ci/policy/worklist-env-registry.json, so a registry plant (test_dropping_a_registered_name_reds, test_a_registered_name_nobody_reads_reds) never writes the tracked file -- that write-mutate-restore shape corrupted it twice in one session when an unrelated kill landed in the write window. Unset means the real registry is read unchanged.

WORKLIST_SCHED_RED_TTL_S.why: How long wl_schedred's shared scheduled-run cache stays fresh, wl_schedred.py:32. Fifteen minutes keeps a GitHub read to about four an hour across every session while a red still surfaces within one stop of the cache expiring.

WORKLIST_SESSION_ID.why: The session identity, tried before CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in wl_core.py:313. Returns "" for CANNOT VERIFY, and the honest response to that is to say nothing rather than accuse, so a typo turns identity checking off without a word.

WORKLIST_SOURCE_OVERRIDE_FILE.why: GATE-SEAM, test-only: `rel/path:override/file`, read by check:ci-worklist-env-registry's own scan_corpus() to substitute one tracked source file's CONTENT with a tmp copy during the plant tests, so test_a_typo_in_a_real_source_file_reds never writes the real tracked file it names. Unset means no substitution: the real corpus is scanned unchanged.

WORKLIST_EPICS_LEDGER.why: read only by a TypeScript gate, as the seam that points its ledger reader at a /tmp fixture. This registry's scan reads Python and bash, so `names` cannot hold it without reporting it DEAD; it lives here so its class still renders into env-manifest, and the gate proves the reader still names it
